verdictVocabulary.pass: meets the rule as rendered, no caveats
verdictVocabulary.fixable: misses the rule but the fix is known and cheap -- note MUST say what
verdictVocabulary.fail: misses the rule, ships broken if unaddressed
verdictVocabulary.unreviewed: not yet judged by a human or fresh-context agent -- the template default

items.rule: If a reference figure is being followed: which stage is this -- REPRODUCE (faithful copy), REPAIR (fix what the reference does badly), or ADAPT (this paper's own figure)? A stage-1 reproduction must NOT ship; an adaptation must not still be a copy.

Pure-black #000000 text on a white canvas. Fills are a LAYERED system -- white, light gray, or a semantic tint are all correct; a grouping may also be a borderless tint field, a dashed boundary, or a gray wedge backplate.

Each hue holds a STABLE ROLE (not one global meaning): saturated/gray = active/inactive, warm tint = the special or selected subsystem, red = the exceptional structural accent ONLY. Ordinary outlines and routine connectors stay black/gray; fills may carry the semantic roles.
No gradient/shadow/glow/3D/photo texture. Flat semantic pictograms ARE the vocabulary and are encouraged. Corners modestly rounded but still read as rectangles -- never a pill or a glassy bubble.

Structural card outlines and ordinary process connectors use 1-2 weights; pictograms, wireless marks and legend swatches carry their own geometry and are OUTSIDE that budget. Emphasis = a thicker stroke or the accent colour, never a dark fill.

One serif family (Times-like) matching the paper body; roughly 3-4 restrained size levels (a dense overview may use more); ONE idea per card; vertical labels are whole words rotated, never letter-stacked.

Stable meaningful pictograms -- the same icon means the same entity every time, and MORE THAN ONE recurring identity glyph is normal. Recurring pictograms need no legend; a non-self-evident colour/link encoding earns a compact FRAMELESS key; a one-off icon must be labelled.

Judge by figure TYPE: a mechanism-detail figure is spacious with large text; a system/overview figure is legitimately VERY dense and must NOT be cleaned up into airy uniformity. The invariant is concise local text + explicit grouping + readable separation of the major flows.

Self-evident spine (or row-major fold). Semantic panel HEADINGS are allowed -- framed, bold on a tint field, or floated beside a stage; what is banned is a detached narrative title or caption sentence. The three observed dashed roles (grouping / spatial region / comparison level) need no legend.

No explanatory SENTENCES or paragraphs on the canvas -- short descriptive fragments and noun phrases are normal and expected. The test is: does it NARRATE? A fragment names a thing; a sentence explains it.

Symbols and short words label the MAJOR units. Compact maths is allowed in six classes only (symbol/function label, parameter value, branch condition, bookkeeping update, ratio, count/coordinate/unit). A DEFINING equation or a decomposition of a research quantity NEVER appears -- it belongs in the caption.
Whole-canvas balance at print scale: no dead zones / empty regions left once every box individually passes rule 7.
At a glance the eye actually follows the intended flow -- the holistic read, not just the structural self-evidence rule 8 encodes.
Every edge label is unambiguous about which arrow it names -- no near-miss with a neighboring edge or label.
Every semantic distinction (hue-encoded meaning, dashed-vs-solid, emphasis stroke) still reads once the figure is converted to grayscale.
